qemu_5.bin - real Hextile payloads from a live QEMU VNC server
============================================================================

WHY THIS FILE EXISTS
A Hextile decoder once read the sub-encoding byte as sequential ids
0,1,2,3,4 instead of the flag mask 0x01,0x02,0x04,0x08,0x10. 261 tests
passed, because every fixture had been generated from that decoder's own
assumptions; nothing had ever compared against bytes a real server sent.
This file is bytes a real server put on the wire.

PROVENANCE - read this before treating it as a corpus
This is ONE screen, from ONE guest, at ONE moment. It is a regression
fixture, not a corpus. It covers 1 Hextile rectangle(s) of a single
full-screen update. It does NOT cover incremental damage updates,
multi-rectangle updates, edge tiles on a resolution that is not a
multiple of 16, cursor pseudo-encodings, other pixel formats, other
guests, or any other server. One real-world sample is a regression guard,
not evidence of general coverage. Re-capturing will produce different
bytes, because the guest's screen is not the same twice.

CAPTURED
date              : 2026-10-09 17:51:52 UTC
server            : QEMU, VNC on 127.0.0.1:6000
desktop name      : QEMU (omarchy)
resolution        : 1280x800
security          : None (RFC 6143 security type 1, no password)
client            : aurora-vnc vnc-client, via an in-process recording proxy

ENCODINGS REQUESTED (SetEncodings, in this order)
5    Hextile, listed first so the server prefers it
0    Raw, mandatory per RFC 6143 7.7.1, present as the fallback
Every rectangle stored below is encoding 5; the capture aborts if
the server sends anything else, so the file cannot silently fill with
the wrong encoding.

PIXEL FORMAT
Requested by the client with SetPixelFormat, not left to the server
default:
bits-per-pixel   : 32
depth            : 24
big-endian-flag  : 0
true-colour-flag : 1
red/green/blue max   : 255/255/255
red/green/blue shift : 16/8/0
Four little-endian bytes per pixel in B, G, R, x order - byte-identical
to Continuum's PixelFormat::BGRX32 and aurora's PixelFormat::RGBX8888_LE.

FILE LAYOUT (all integers big-endian)
0        magic      4 bytes  "CVF1"
4        count      u16      number of rectangles
6        rectangles count x ( x:u16 y:u16 w:u16 h:u16 len:u32 payload:len )
trailer  width     u32      1280
trailer  height    u32      800
`payload` is the rectangle's encoding payload only, with no 12-byte
rectangle header, matching what a decoder is handed after parsing the
header out of a FramebufferUpdate.

SIZE
rectangles        : 1
payload bytes     : 66611
file bytes        : 66637

CAPTURE TOOL
continuum-transport/examples/capture_vnc_fixture.rs. Read-only: it sends
SetPixelFormat, SetEncodings and non-incremental
FramebufferUpdateRequest messages and nothing else. It never sends a
key, pointer, clipboard, resize or shutdown message, and never touches
QMP.

The client half is aurora-vnc's vnc-client rather than a hand-rolled
RFC 6143 implementation. A hand-rolled client written for this task
completed the handshake against this QEMU but never received an update
once it had sent SetEncodings, while aurora's received one immediately;
the raw bytes are therefore taken through an in-process recording proxy
spliced in front of the server, and cut out of the recording with
aurora's own hextile_len / payload_len so the framing used to capture is
the framing the fixture is replayed through.

Before writing, the tool replays the extracted rectangles through
aurora's decoder and checks the result is pixel-identical to the frame
the client had already built, so a mis-cut rectangle cannot be checked
in.

Incidental during this session: 0 Bell, 0
SetColourMapEntries, 0 ServerCutText message(s) were skipped.
